alate: Head reddish brown, the postclypeus pale yellowish brown, the anteclypeus white, the antennae brown, the pronotum slightly darker than the head and with a T-shaped mark, each anterolateral corner with an ocellus-like ring-shaped spot. Head semicircular, the fontanelle small and round, the compound eyes not very round and slightly projecting outwards, the ocelli broadly oval, the ocellus-compound eye distance about equal to the short diameter of the ocellus; the postclypeus about half as long as wide with longitudinal striae in the middle, the anteclypeus trapezoidal, the labrum arcuate, the antennae with 19 segments. As to the body pilosity, short hairs are densely distributed over the head and postclypeus, interspersed with sparse long hairs; several hairs arise in the middle of the labrum; the pronotum is densely covered with fine pubescence.
soldier: Head orange-yellow, the mandibles dark brown with deep yellow bases; setae on the head sparse, about ten stout long erect bristles around the margin of the labrum, the pilosity of the thoracic and abdominal tergites sparse. Head oval, narrow anteriorly and broad posteriorly, longer than wide, widest in the posterior part. Labrum lingulate, its apex bluntly rounded, reaching one-third of the base of the open mandibles. Mandibles sickle-shaped and rather robust, the apices incurved; the left marginal tooth at about one-third from the anterior end, the right mandible with a dot-like small tooth slightly below the corresponding position. Antennae with 17 segments, segment 3 short and small. Postmentum rectangular, slightly narrower anteriorly and broader posteriorly, less than twice as long as wide. The anterior half of the pronotum is narrow and nearly vertically upturned, the posterior half broader, and both the anterior and the posterior margin have a distinct median notch.
